metadata.title: Don't expect to see SpaceX on the S&P 500 so soon after IPO

content.text:
S&P Dow Jones Indices stated that it will not be changing its rules to fast-track SpaceX (SPAX.PVT) and other mega-IPOs into the S&P 500 index (^GSPC).
Morning Brief Host Julie Hyman and Vanity Fair contributing editor Bethany McLean discuss SpaceX's valuation in the lead up to the space company's public launch a week from now.
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) CEO Jamie Dimon hosted Elon Musk as part of SpaceX's (SPAX.PVT) pre-IPO roadshow, as the company sets its sights on an IPO price of $135 per share next Friday, June 12.
It is interesting in that context to not see S&P Dow Jones joining the, you know, what we have seen in terms of the of Nasdaq and some of the other index providers changing their rules. So,
it it raises a really interesting potential that you will have, you know, the SPY and the other ETFs and indexes that are um indexed to the S&P 500, not having SpaceX. And the Nasdaq products will include SpaceX in short order. And we, you know, we were sort of joking in the run-up to the SpaceX IPO for the people who don't want it, like would would there be ex SpaceX products that the ETF world comes out with. Well, it turns out S&P doesn't have to do that because it's already going to be an ex um SpaceX product. So, it'll be interesting to see sort of like who is right, right, in terms of performance. Um, you know, because there are pitfalls to including something like a SpaceX.
I'm actually really happy to see that that news and one of the reasons is someone a long-time source of mine had described the situation to me with SpaceX being part of uh of of the S&P 500 as the mother of all short squeezes. Because what would have happened is that index funds would have had to own uh SpaceX as a result. And because of the small float, you would have had this stock that was completely driven by by short squeezes. and I think that's an unhealthy dynamic. And so I'm glad to see the I'm glad to see the market giving a little bit of time to absorb this rather than forcing that situation where you had forced buyers of SpaceX.
Right. Um, pretty much every sort of financial advisor that we've had on has said wait, right? That that's the advice they're giving to their clients, wait for it to be public a little while, see what happens with it. Even if you belong, or even if you believe in the long-term story, there'll be an opportunity later to get in. You don't have to get in right away because like, you know, yes, they're sending rockets up now, but the rocket still doesn't hasn't met the goal that they wanted to meet in terms of the amount of payload. Starlink is the part of the business that's working, but there's a lot of the business that still we, you know, has has yet to prove its uh its potential, shall we say?
Yeah. So I was just going to ask you, what do you think the story is? I was thinking about it's sort of a version of that Churchill play, right? about Russia, a riddle wrapped in an enigma, wrapped in a something or another. But um, I think of that as a good description of SpaceX, right? It's a profitable satellite internet company wrapped in a, um wrapped in the sexiness of a space company and then wrapped in this giant riddle of what XAI is actually worth. And I think there was a recent uh financial Times piece pointing out just how much of the valuation is being driven by this these forecasts on the part of Goldman among others for enormous growth in XAI. I think uh the revenue is supposed to be up 10 times to to or 100 times, these astronomical absolutely astronomical revenue growth predictions for XAI, which is a business that isn't quite not only is it not working, um um um well in comparison to the others, but even if it were working well, there's a lot of questions about the fundamental long-term profitability of these of of these businesses. So it really is a more massive bet than I think people necessarily realize and a more indefinitely a bet on Musk given that he controls what 80 to 85% of the voting shares. It's as if he took a lesson from Tesla and said, wait, wait, wait, I want to make sure I am completely in charge.
Oh, listen, totally. He explicitly took took that lesson.
